newsitem.title: INDONESIA: FOCUS-Indonesia rupiah, stock market plunge.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Indonesia rupiah, stock market plunge.

text.p: The Indonesian rupiah on Monday suffered its largest-ever single-day loss, plunging about 140 points to an historic low against the dollar in the latest in a series of attacks on exotic currencies, dealers said.
The rupiah sank to a 2,650/55 low against the dollar from a 2,510/20 open before some support emerged, traders said.
The panic spread to the Jakarta stock market, where the composite index fell about 1.6 percent to 712.11 points in late morning trade before recovering marginally to 713.35 points at midsession.
One Japanese bank dealer said the dollar was taken once at the 2,650 level but some offers seemed to at least temporarily halt the U.S. currency from breaking the fragile resistance.
"The target is clear. Speculators want to test the (central bank's intervention) band at the 2,681 level," the dealer said.
The intervention band was set at 2,377/2,681 on Friday.
Other traders said the bank had made some inquiries about prevailing prices but had not yet intervened.
They said volumes were thin but the attack on the currency was concerted.
"The market is not hectic but nervous. Each time a price was taken, the next price was five points higher," one dealer said.
"It's simply contagion," said Desmond Supple, exotic currencies specialist at BZW Barclays in Singapore. "It's the continuation of a trend which started with the Thai baht."
"All current-account deficit currencies are particularly vulnerable," he added, pointing to attacks last week on the Philippine peso and the Malaysian ringgit and on currencies in South America.
Thailand and the Philippines announced de facto devaluations of their currencies earlier this month in the face of relentless pressure from speculators.

Supple said testing of the central bank band would continue into the week, although the I.D.E.A. consultancy said regional weakness should cool down after a meeting of Asian central bank chiefs in Shanghai on Friday.

"We expect some stern verbal intervention against speculators," the consultancy said in a report. "This, or at least the fear of such statements, should help to cap regional weakness later this week."
It added that if the rupiah plunged to the lower end of the band, that would imply a fall of 13.6 percent in the currency.
"With the other regionals, namely Thailand and the Philippines down more than 20 percent and more 10 percent, respectively, there is definitely such a possibility," it said.
